name: etf_nav_arbitrage_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: NIFTY 50 ETFs (e.g., NIFTYBEES) frequently trade at a premium or discount to their real-time indicative NAV (iNAV) due to stale limit orders, low ETF market-maker activity during volatile periods, and retail order flow that pushes ETF prices away from fair value. In India, ETF market-making is less competitive than in the US, creating persistent intraday premium/discount cycles of 10-30 bps that mean-revert as authorized participants (APs) step in. The inefficiency persists because AP arbitrage has minimum lot sizes and creation/redemption friction, leaving small premium/discount windows exploitable by fast retail traders.
indicators: iNAV = real_time_indicative_NAV (computed from NIFTY 50 component prices)

conditions: premium_discount < -15 (ETF trading at >15bps discount to NAV)
long.confirmation: premium_discount narrows by 2bps from trough (AP activity starting)

conditions: premium_discount > 15 (ETF trading at >15bps premium to NAV)

entry.entry_price: limit order at current best bid (long) or best ask (short)

exit.stop_loss: premium_discount widens to 30bps against position OR loss > 0.3%
exit.trailing_stop: once premium_discount within 5bps of zero, trail stop at 10bps from best
exit.signal_exit: if etf_volume_ratio drops below 0.2 (liquidity drying up), exit at market

filters.vix_filter: when VIX > 25, increase premium_discount threshold to 25bps (wider dislocations needed)
filters.time_filter: best signals 09:30-11:00 and 14:00-15:00; avoid lunch hour 12:00-13:30
filters.event_filter: skip on NIFTY rebalancing days; caution on F&O expiry
other_filters: skip if iNAV data feed is stale (last update > 30 seconds ago)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — as Indian ETF market matures and more market makers enter, premiums/discounts will shrink

weaknesses: iNAV computation depends on real-time prices of all 50 components; any staleness in component feeds creates false premium/discount signals
NIFTYBEES has lower liquidity than the underlying stocks; large positions face significant market impact and wide spreads during volatile periods
Short selling ETFs on NSE may not always be feasible for retail; strategy effectiveness is halved if only long-discount trades are taken
prior_art: Petajisto (2017) ETF mispricing; Madhavan (2014) ETF arbitrage mechanics. Adapted for Indian ETF market where premium/discount is structurally wider than US due to fewer authorized participants.
notes: Edge math: 0.68 * 25bps - 0.32 * 20bps = 17 - 6.4 = 10.6bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~1.6bps/trade * 4 trades = ~6.4bps daily. 22bps estimate includes occasional 30+ bps dislocation trades. Key risk is iNAV accuracy — garbage in, garbage out.
